title: Optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization overhead, thread-pool pinning, and continuous-batching improvements
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: production workloads observed CPU-side tail latency spikes under high QPS for small requests. Investigation showed time spent in request serialization, thread-pool overhead, and contention when pins were not set for CPU-bound work. This PR reduces serialization copies, introduces lightweight per-request buffers, adds an affinity-aware thread pool variant for CPU inference paths, and tightens continuous-batching heuristics to avoid unnecessary wakeups. The change set is modular: 1) request_path: remove redundant message copies and use zero-copy span wrappers for proto/json handling; 2) threadpool: add AffinityThreadPool with optional core pinning and work-stealing between NUMA nodes; 3) kv-cache: make reads lock-free for hot-key access paths and add microbenchmark; 4) batching: avoid spinning when batch sizes are already optimal and add an adaptive backoff based on observed seq-len distribution. Benchmarks: microbench shows 18-26% p50/p95 CPU latency improvement on c6i-like instances and 12% throughput uplift for mixed-length streaming workloads at the same latency SLO. Rollout plan: smoke in staging, canary 5% in us-west1, full rollout pending perf dashboard validation. Related: ENG-2345 (reduce request path tail), SUP-1123 (customer-reported tail latency).

diff_snippets: runtime/src/request_path.cpp: replaced memcpy-based serialization with RequestSpan::wrap(view) to avoid intermediate allocations
runtime/src/threadpool/affinity_threadpool.cc: add SetThreadAffinity(core) with fallback when OS lacks API
runtime/src/kv_cache/hotpath.cc: use atomic stamped pointers for lock-free reads; keep slow-path locked update
serving/continuous_batcher.cpp: changed spin-wait to condition-variable with exponential backoff capped by 5ms

performance_summary: Microbench: p50 CPU latency reduced by 18%, p95 reduced by 26% for small seq-length requests. End-to-end canary (5% traffic): 12% higher throughput at same latency SLO. KV cache fallback rate <0.5% under targeted load. Memory overhead: +1.8% due to small per-thread buffers when affinity pool enabled.
rollback_plan: Feature gated via runtime.threadpool.affinity_enabled; immediate rollback: disable flag and cleanup configs. If KV fallback issues observed, revert commit runtime/src/kv_cache/hotpath.cc to previous lock-protected path (patch available in branch).
release_notes: Performance: Reduced CPU request-path latency and improved throughput by optimizing serialization, adding an affinity-aware thread pool, lock-free KV cache hot-path reads, and tuning continuous-batching backoff. Configs: runtime.threadpool.affinity_enabled=false by default; enable after validation. Metrics: kv.hotpath.fallback_count added.
merge_details: Merged after reviewers approved and CI green. Canary rollout started 2026-02-20 in us-west1 at 5% traffic. Monitoring dashboards linked in issue ENG-2345.
notes: This PR targets CPU-bound request workloads; GPU serving customers unaffected. Ops: recommend enabling affinity pool on homogeneous CPU fleets only; monitor pinned thread CPU saturation metrics before wide rollout.
